subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which programming construct repeats a block of statements?
questions.explain: Iteration (looping) causes a block of statements to be repeated.

questions.q: Which keyword typically begins a selection statement in Python?
questions.explain: Selection is implemented with an if statement that runs code when a condition is true.

questions.q: A count-controlled loop is best described as one that...
options: repeats a set number of times
repeats until the user presses a key
questions.explain: A count-controlled loop (e.g. a for loop) runs a fixed, known number of times.

questions.q: Which loop is most appropriate when the number of repetitions is not known in advance?
questions.explain: A condition-controlled while loop keeps repeating until a condition is met, so the count need not be known beforehand.

questions.q: What is printed by: for i in range(1, 4): print(i)?
questions.explain: range(1, 4) produces 1, 2 and 3, stopping before the end value 4.

questions.q: Which data type would be used to store a person's age in whole years?
questions.explain: An integer stores whole numbers such as an age with no fractional part.

questions.q: Which data type stores only the values True or False?
questions.explain: A Boolean can hold only one of two values: True or False.

questions.q: Which data type stores numbers that have a decimal (fractional) part?
questions.explain: A real (float) data type stores numbers with a fractional part, such as 3.14.

questions.q: An array is a data structure that stores...
options: multiple values of the same data type under one identifier
several fields of different data types
questions.explain: An array holds many elements of the same type, accessed by an index under one name.

questions.q: Why might a two-dimensional array be used?
options: To store data in rows and columns, such as a grid
To store a single Boolean value
To store one item of text
To store the remainder of a division
questions.explain: A 2D array organises data into rows and columns, useful for grids and tables.

questions.q: Which Python function reads data typed in by the user?
questions.explain: The input() function captures data entered by the user at the keyboard.

questions.q: The MOD operator returns the...
questions.explain: MOD (modulus) gives the remainder left after integer division.

questions.q: In Python, what is the difference between = and ==?
options: = assigns a value, == tests whether two values are equal
questions.explain: = is the assignment operator, while == is the comparison operator that checks equality.

questions.q: What is the value of 17 MOD 5?
questions.explain: 17 divided by 5 is 3 remainder 2, so 17 MOD 5 is 2.

questions.q: What is the value of the expression 3 + 4 * 2?
questions.explain: Multiplication is evaluated before addition, so 4 * 2 = 8, then 3 + 8 = 11.

questions.q: A subprogram that returns a value is called a...
questions.explain: A function is a named subprogram that carries out a task and returns a value.

questions.q: Which keyword is used to define a subprogram in Python?
questions.explain: The def keyword defines a function or procedure in Python.

questions.q: What is a key benefit of using subprograms?
options: Code can be reused, reducing repetition and making programs easier to maintain
Programs always run faster on every machine
They remove the need for variables
questions.explain: Subprograms allow reusable, modular code that avoids repetition and is easier to test and maintain.

questions.q: What is a parameter in a subprogram?
options: A value passed into the subprogram for it to use
The value the subprogram sends back
questions.explain: A parameter is a variable that receives a value (argument) passed into the subprogram when it is called.

questions.q: Given def add(a, b): return a + b, what does add(3, 4) return?
questions.explain: The arguments 3 and 4 are passed in and the function returns their sum, 7.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Computer Science (1CP2) specification; Problem Solving With Programming
